Description

We’re looking for a hands-on (Senior) Electromagnetic Development Engineer to support the development of our systems across magnetic and RF domains and other simulations, e.g. of thermal effects. In this role, you will combine simulation, lab validation, and engineering feedback to improve product performance from prototype to deployment. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to identify electromagnetic issues early, validate concepts in the lab, and translate findings into practical design improvements.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

 

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

 
 

What will you do

  • Develop and run electromagnetic simulations for magnetic and RF systems in industrial machines

  • Analyze and optimize components and system behavior, including coils, shielding, antennas, cabling, and subsystem interactions

  • Investigate electromagnetic effects on machines and assemblies during integration, testing, and operation

  • Identify and mitigate EMI/EMC, coupling, and interference issues across electrical and mechanical interfaces

  • Translate findings into concrete design improvements and provide feedback to electrical, mechanical, and system engineering

  • Support product development from design through integration, validation, and certification readiness

 

What is expected of you

  • Strong background in electrical engineering, physics, or a related field

  • Several years of hands-on experience in electromagnetic simulation and development in an industrial environment on system level

  • Good understanding of electromagnetic theory and simulation methods such as FEM, FDTD

  • Power user of simulation tools like Ansys HFSS, Maxwell, Icepak or similar

  • Practical experience with measurement, testing, and validation of electromagnetic behavior on real systems

  • Familiarity with EMI/EMC requirements

  • Experience with development processes related to CE, SEMI, UL or IEC 61010 compliance is a strong plus

  • Ability to derive pragmatic engineering solutions and work effectively across disciplines

 

Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

  • Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together.

 

About us

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

Engineered for performance, our stack leverages PyTorch for model training, NVIDIA Triton to achieve sub-100ms inference. Here, you will find the autonomy, the data depth, and the massive scale required to solve the most complex optimization challenges in the adtech ecosystem.

The data infrastructure behind this runs at real scale: 2TB ingested in real time every day, 100+ Airflow jobs and data pipelines, and ML models handling p99 latency of 100ms across 100,000+ predictions per second.

We need someone who can rigorously evaluate models through offline experiments and A/B tests before they hit our 100,000+ predictions-per-second production environment.

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
We're building the AI operating system for vets. Our AI agent Emma already runs client communication for clinics in 7 countries, including the largest veterinary groups in the world. As Customer Success Manager, you make sure every clinic gets the most out of Emma, from the first setup to the day they can't imagine working without her.

About Vetpal

There are more pets than ever, and fewer vets to care for them. Clinics are short on staff, vets spend half their day on admin, and their suicide rate is six times higher than average. We're building the AI operating system for vets. From the first phone call to the invoice, we give vets their time back, with the mission to bring pets, pet owners and their vets closer together.

The role

You own the relationship with our clinics once they've signed. You onboard new practices, set up Emma so she fits the way each clinic works, and become the person practice teams call when they have a question or an idea. You're the bridge between vets and our product: you explain a technical product in the language of everyday practice life, and you bring what you hear back to our engineers. You work closely with the founders and the rest of our CS team.

What you'll work on

  • Onboard new clinics and configure Emma to match their workflows, phone setup and practice software

  • Be the go-to contact for your clinics, from small practices to large clinic groups

  • Run trainings and regular check-ins so practice teams use Emma every day

  • Keep an eye on account health, spot risks early and find opportunities to grow accounts

  • Solve customer questions fast and hand technical issues to engineering with the right details

  • Turn customer feedback into clear input for our product team

  • Help build our CS playbook, help center and processes as we scale across Europe

Who thrives here

  • You genuinely enjoy talking to customers, on the phone, on site and in writing

  • You're technically curious, understand how software, integrations and phone systems fit together, and can explain them simply to a busy practice team

  • You bring experience in customer success or account management, ideally in B2B SaaS

  • Big plus: you're a trained veterinary nurse (TFA) or have worked in a vet practice yourself, so you know practice life from the inside

  • You're structured and reliable, and you keep your accounts and CRM clean

  • You speak fluent German and English, more languages are a plus

What we offer

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • A role you can shape from day one as we build out customer success

  • A small, talent-dense team in Berlin that works with speed and intensity

Build with us

Businesses deserve better from finance. Less friction, more freedom. Since 2004, Mollie has been on a mission to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies trust our all-in-one platform to get paid, manage money and grow on their terms. Simple, scalable and built with real businesses in mind.

Your impact

You'll run kickoffs with internal and external stakeholders, set go live dates, keep progress on track, and coordinate testing and feedback along the way. This function is newly formed, so you'll have real influence over how the role and its processes take shape, bringing in your own experience rather than following a fixed playbook. The role is also more technical than it might first appear: you'll get close to the real world edge cases and issues that surface once a solution meets implementation reality, giving you hands on technical exposure without needing a payments or engineering background going in.

Your work protects revenue by keeping live dates on track, and it supports how Mollie scales delivery more broadly, building a structured, dedicated integration phase for its biggest deals. You'll report to Jan-Jaap van Helden.

 

What you'll ship

  • Own the post sales integration phase for Mollie's largest and most complex deals, from handover through testing to go live

  • Run kickoffs with internal and external stakeholders, setting go live dates and keeping progress on track

  • Organise and track testing, raising issues and feedback as they surface

  • Coordinate across sales, product and engineering colleagues, as well as with merchants directly, to keep everyone aligned

  • Keep agreed go live dates on track, since delays mean missed revenue

  • Maintain documentation and playbooks that make delivery predictable and scalable

     

What you'll bring

  • Strong organisational and structuring skills, with solid project management ability

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

title: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting
description:
Prevention Analyst - Pentesting

About this role


We are looking for a Prevention Analyst - Pentester, to join our Prevention track. An attacker does not look at one server in isolation. They look at everything a company exposes to the internet and work out where to start. You will do the same for our clients, taking the attacker’s view of their external attack surface, seeing what an attacker sees, and doing what an attacker would do next.

That means reading the story behind an attack surface. A forgotten subdomain, an old login portal, and a misconfigured mail server may each look minor on their own. Together they can show how an organisation has grown, where its blind spots are, and where someone could get in. When you find a potential weak point, you dig into it technically to find out how far an attacker could actually go.

This is not a classic penetration testing role. The deep dive draws on pentest methodology and expertise, but it is not a full pentest, and you will not spend your weeks writing long reports. We focus on finding the high impact vulnerabilities that need attention now and getting them to the client in a form they can act on.

This is for someone with hands on pentesting experience who wants to work across many customer environments, sharpen their attacker mindset, and grow into owning complex prevention engagements end to end.

What you will do

  • Assess clients’ external attack surface as a whole, from the attacker’s perspective.

  • Identify gaps and weaknesses across the surface, not just within a single asset, and work out how they connect.

  • Run technical deep dives into potential weak points to establish how far an attacker could get in practice.

  • Separate what needs fixing now from what does not, and focus on high and critical findings with immediate impact.

  • Turn technical findings into short, clear advice that clients can understand and act on.

  • Share what you learn with the team and actively pick up what others know. We work on problems together.

description:
What We Do

Rillet serves accounting and finance teams, the financial brains of their companies. Our job is to help them run the numbers with impossible speed, accuracy, and insight.

Rillet is the Agentic ERP built for modern finance teams. We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.

We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.

Who We Are

Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.

The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.

Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan.

Rillet is built on deep accounting expertise, and it takes people from many disciplines to build a category-defining company. You do not need to be an accountant to thrive here. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Together, we combine the precision of accounting with the speed, creativity, and ambition of AI-native software to power the financial core of the world’s fastest-growing companies while redefining what finance teams should expect from their software.

The Role

We have grown quickly, and our Solution Consulting team is at the center of how prospects evaluate Rillet as their next ERP. We are looking for a Solution Consulting Manager to lead and scale that team.

This is a player-coach role weighted heavily toward coaching. You will spend roughly 25% of your time running your own sales cycles (staying sharp, credible and close to the customer and product) and roughly 75% of your time coaching, mentoring and developing your team, primarily by riding shotgun on live deals and giving real-time feedback. You will also be a key voice in shaping the product and building the Solution Consulting infrastructure that lets the organization scale.

You will work directly with the CEO, GTM leadership and the Product team.

Responsibilities

Coach, mentor and develop the team (~75%)

  • Ride shotgun on deals. Join discovery calls, demos, technical validations and POCs to observe, step in when needed, and give specific, real-time feedback. Run tight pre-call prep and post-call debriefs so every deal is a learning opportunity.

  • Raise the bar on craft. Coach Solution Consultants on discovery, value selling, storytelling, demo design, handling technical objections, and tailoring sandbox environments to each customer's use cases.

  • Grow each person individually. Set clear expectations and development plans, give regular honest feedback, and help each Solution Consultant build deep product and accounting domain expertise and advance in their career.

  • Hire and onboard. Recruit, interview and ramp new Solution Consultants, and build an onboarding program that gets them deal-ready quickly.

  • Partner on deal strategy. Work with Account Executives and sales leadership to staff deals, pressure-test strategy on complex ERP evaluations, and keep technical wins on track.

Run your own sales cycles (~25%)

  • Remove technical objections. Take on strategic and complex opportunities, understanding the prospect's business requirements and existing technology stack, and clearly articulating how Rillet integrates and improves their processes.

  • Deliver high-impact demos. Set up and tailor the sandbox environment, answer questions in real time, and act as the prospect's trusted consultant throughout the purchase process.

  • Represent Rillet. Be the face of the company, applying high customer empathy and structured problem-solving to ensure every prospect interaction is excellent, including with finance and accounting leaders.

Inform product and build for scale

  • Be the voice of the prospect. Synthesize front-line feedback, objections, competitive intel and feature gaps from across the team, and bring it to founders and Product in close to real time, with clear patterns and prioritization.

  • Influence the roadmap. Partner with Product on discovery, early feedback on new features, and how capabilities are positioned and demoed.

  • Build Solution Consulting infrastructure. Create the systems, playbooks and tools that help the team scale, such as discovery frameworks, demo standards and reusable assets, sandbox and demo-data templates, technical FAQs and objection libraries, POC and technical-validation processes, a deal-review cadence, and enablement and certification paths.

  • Measure what matters. Define and track team metrics (technical win rate, ramp time, deal coverage, cycle time) and use them to improve how the team operates.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years managing or formally mentoring pre-sales, solutions consulting or sales engineering teams, with a track record of developing people.

  • 3+ years of industry accounting experience across areas such as revenue recognition, month-end close and multi-entity consolidation.

  • 3+ years supporting complex ERP sales cycles with implementation and/or customer support for accounting or financial solutions.

  • Deep knowledge of the ecosystem of tools in the office of the CFO.

  • Excellent communicator who makes complex concepts easy to understand, and who can give direct, constructive feedback in the moment.

  • Experience building processes, enablement or tooling for a growing team, ideally in an early-stage, fast-moving environment.

  • Thrives in a dynamic environment while keeping high attention to detail.

  • CPA certification or having started your career in audit is a plus.

Note: All official Rillet recruiting communications will come from an @rillet.com email address. If you’re contacted from another domain, please disregard the message and report it as spam.

Life at Rillet

title: Software Development Engineer in Test II, NavNative
description:
Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 

What We Do

The Navigation Native team builds the high-performance C++ engine that serves as the "brain" of our Navigation SDKs. This library runs directly on end-user systems (on-board), powering everything from mobile apps to in-vehicle infotainment systems for partners like BMW, Porsche, and Zeekr.

We solve the fundamental challenges of movement: transforming noisy GPS/IMU data into precise map-matching, managing complex road-network graphs, supporting routes and alternatives, tracking progress along a route, and providing "Electronic Horizon" capabilities for ADAS. Our work happens at the edge, supporting location frequencies up to 10Hz and ensuring a seamless experience even in tunnels or dense urban canyons.

As AI becomes embedded in modern engineering workflows, we value engineers who can thoughtfully integrate AI into design, development, and decision-making. Our interview process will include discussion of how you use AI in your engineering workflow.

What You'll Do

We are looking for smart, fast-learning engineers who care as much about proving that navigation works as about making it work. As an SDE(T), you will:

  • Build and maintain the unit, integration, and functional test architecture for a C++17 library, and the CMake and CI pipelines that run it.

  • Turn real-world location recordings into regression tests, and define the quality metrics for map-matching, routing, and route-following.

  • Keep the quality signal fast and trustworthy: eliminate flaky tests, run sanitizer and performance builds, and track coverage.

  • Build AI-driven test tooling: agent-based test generation, automated dogfooding and triage, and AI-assisted PR review.

  • Partner with feature engineers on testability and review designs for how they will be verified.

  • Thoughtfully leverage AI tools in your workflow and set the standard for how the team uses them. 

What We Believe Are Important Traits for This Role

  •  5+ years of experience in C++17: comfortable writing test code and tooling, reading production code, and debugging with sanitizers and profilers. Python or similar for harnesses and analysis.

  • Proven experience building test infrastructure for a large native codebase: test frameworks, CMake, and CI systems.

  • A data-driven mindset: you define metrics, build the tooling to measure them, and use them to argue for or against a change.

  • Experience diagnosing hard-to-reproduce failures: flakiness, platform-specific behavior, memory and threading bugs.

  • Strong English skills, with the ability to explain test results, risk, and trade-offs to peers and stakeholders.

Would be a Plus

  • Familiarity with navigation concepts (map matching, dead reckoning, route progress, or Electronic Horizon).

  • Experience with replay- or simulation-based testing using real sensor and GPS data.

  • Hands-on experience building AI- or agent-based developer tooling for testing, code review, or triage.

  • Experience with coverage tooling, performance benchmarking, or testing SDKs through generated bindings.


Employment Requirements

  • Employment Type: Full-time

  • Weekly Hours: 40 h per week

  • Location/Hybrid Policy: Remote (from any city in Germany)

    What We Value

In addition to our core values, which are not unique to this position and are necessary for Mapbox leaders:

  • We value high-performing creative individuals who dig into problems and opportunities.

  • We believe in individuals being their whole selves at work. We commit to this through supportive health care, parental leave, flexibility for the things that come up in life, and innovating on how we think about supporting our people.

  • We emphasize an environment of teaching and learning to equip employees with the tools needed to be successful in their function and the company.

  • We strongly believe in the value of growing a diverse team and encourage people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, abilities, and sexual orientations to apply.

How We Support You

  • Hybrid/Remote Options: Enjoy flexibility to work comfortably from home or periodically from an office where applicable.

  • Country-Specific Care & Coverage: Private health, dental, and income protection plans tailored to elevate your regional statutory benefits.

  • Family-First Support: Family care, maternity and paternity leave policies to support your growing family.

  • Lifestyle Spending Account: Contributions to support your health, wellness, and personal growth.

  • Balance & Brainpower: Mental health support for you and your dependents.

  • Rest & Recharge: Paid time away, company holidays, and generous absence policies.

  • Time Off to Give Back: Dedicated paid volunteering time in addition to your standard PTO.

  • Coordinate the data, scenarios and simulation each new operating site needs, so they are ready when the site goes live.

  • Run the layer's cloud cost reporting, and help leads balance cost against keeping available the data that teams need.

  • Track what the teams need from others and what others need from them, raise conflicts early and broker the trade-offs:

Hands-on experience in data engineering, machine learning or simulation is preferred but not essential.

title: Design Engineer
description:
Since early 2024, we've gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We have a big mission: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run and grow a renewables installation business, and through that to make a real dent in the world's carbon emissions and a far better experience for homeowners.

We're now looking for a Design Engineer who wants to design & ship exceptional outcomes for users. Most of our product is a front end over hard physics (heat-loss calculations, hydronic design, LiDAR floor plans, compliance that has to be right), used by installers on a phone, with no signal, in a hurry. Making that feel simple is a design problem and an engineering problem at the same time, and this role sits right on that seam.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have grown the team 3x and revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, are launching an end-to-end solar and battery product in November, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll own how the product looks, feels and behaves wherever installers use it, from the first sketch to the shipped feature. Installers only adopt Spruce if it's easy to use on a real job, and adoption is what drives our growth. That puts your work at the centre of the business. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Designing and shipping – You'll take a flow from rough idea all the way to production, prototyping in whatever gets you to an answer fastest (often code, sometimes Figma or a sketch), and testing with installers as you go. The gap between "we should fix this" and "it's fixed" is often a day.

  • Owning the interaction layer – You'll build and look after the component library and the patterns underneath it: motion, loading and empty states, touch targets that still work with gloves on. The small things that make a complex tool feel simple.

  • Building the parts that are hard to get right – The canvas-based floor plan and system design tools, the offline survey app (incl. LiDAR), the proposals homeowners see. These are the parts where the UI is the product, and where we've got the most still to build.

  • Raising the bar on everything we ship – You'll work closely with our product designers and developers, pairing on their work and reviewing it, so the quality of what you build rubs off on the rest of the product.

  • Spending time with installers – You'll go out on site, watch how the product actually gets used, then come back and change it.

You'll report to Steph, our co-founder and CPO (she’s pretty awesome) and you’ll work alongside Dan & Arron who’ve cooked up some incredible work in their time so far.

 

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You might currently call yourself a designer who ships, a front-end engineer with strong design instincts, or already a design engineer. We're looking for 3+ years of experience (and potentially a lot more) designing and building product UI, ideally in a startup or a fast-paced, impact-focussed team. We'd love to speak with you if you have:

  • Real taste, and shipped work to prove it – You can show us production UI you designed and built, and talk about why the details are the way they are. Work you'd happily put next to the best-crafted B2B products out there.

  • Strong design craft, and a real appetite for code – You're a strong designer first. You don't need to be a front-end engineer, and you might well ship with Cursor or Claude Code, but you want to understand the code you're shipping. Bonus for React and TypeScript depth, canvas/WebGL, animation, or complex state on mobile.

  • A prototyping instinct – You'd rather build a rough version and test it than argue about it in a doc. You're comfortable with things being imperfect in front of users.

  • Systems thinking – You enjoy the structure of a good component library and understand that consistency is what lets a small team ship fast. You also know when to slow down first: you value time spent on lo-fi wireframes and on understanding the data model before anything gets polished.

  • Curiosity about the domain – You want to understand how heating systems, solar and battery actually work, and you pick up technical detail fast. By the end of week two you'll be arguing about the best way to show a homeowner their solar self-consumption.

 

🌟 Our offer

  • 💰 £60-110k salary, depending on experience and location

  • 🍰 Meaningful slice of equity (options) in the company

  • 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

  • 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

  • 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

  • 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)

  • 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

  • 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

 

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

  • We're currently a close-knit team of 34, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

  • You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

  • We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. This is clearly particularly important for this role but you'll be surrounded by a whole team who are also close to our customers.

  • We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what we can learn, and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

  • Feedback is constant, direct, and kind. We'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

title: Production Engineer, Network Engineering
description:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Production Engineering Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Turn every network fault from a mystery into a closed ticket. Link diagnostics across router to router and NIC to router paths, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows what's broken and why, because at 10s of GW scale debugging has to be systematic, not artisanal.

  • Build the network repair pipeline that runs itself. Automated fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver lifecycle tracking, and return to service, across DC fabric, edge, and host to network layers, because a new site comes online every six months and manual repair doesn't keep up.

  • Build the network monitoring platform for a fleet that never stops growing. Alerting lifecycle and health dashboards for infrastructure spanning multiple hyperscale sites today and 10s of GW next year. It doesn't exist yet. We're building it.

Role Scope

  • Carry the on-call pager for the network fleet and run repair end to end: diagnose the fault, execute the fix or drive the RMA, and return the link to service across DC fabric, edge, and host to network layers.

  • Write Python and Go tooling that replaces manual diagnosis, including link tests, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows what's broken and why, so faults resolve in minutes, not hours.

  • Automate the repair pipeline from fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver and optics tracking, and return to service, so a failure at any site follows the same path without manual handoffs.

  • Maintain the realtime monitoring and alerting that gives every on-call engineer a true picture of network health across all sites, and keep it accurate as new sites and hardware roll in.

  • Validate new sites and hardware into production by running the qualification tests that confirm a network is healthy before it carries traffic.

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've carried a pager for a production network and can walk into an outage, find the fault, fix it or drive the RMA, and write the postmortem without someone walking you through it.

  • You've written Python or Go scripts that replaced a manual, repetitive network task, from link diagnostics to config pushes to fleet-wide command execution.

  • You understand how a transceiver fault, a misconfigured route, and a power event each show up differently in the data, and you can tell them apart from the signals alone.

  • You've worked hands-on with link diagnostics, optics, and network monitoring protocols such as gNMI, gRPC, NETCONF, and SONiC, and you're comfortable at the CLI on switches and routers across a fleet.

  • You treat toil as a bug. If a repair step means SSHing into ten boxes by hand, you script it once and never do it by hand again.

  • You reach real competence in an unfamiliar part of the stack fast, and you document what you learn so the next on-call engineer doesn't start from zero.

  • Bonus: RMA and repair lifecycle automation. Large-scale datacenter fabric (BGP, ECMP, spine-leaf). Out-of-band network management. Fluency with AI coding tools such as Claude Code or Cursor to move faster on scripts and tooling.

Salary & Benefits

  • Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).

  • Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.

  • Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.

Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Platform team leads iwoca’s developer experience work. It looks after three areas:

  • Infrastructure. iwoca’s Kubernetes platform, GitOps deployments, CI components, and developer environments.

  • The route to production. The templates, tooling, and safe defaults teams use to go from a repository to production and run their own services.

  • The AI platform. Access to the latest models, an internal Claude Code plugin marketplace, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers that connect AI tools to iwoca’s systems.

The Platform team is part of Core Systems, a group of about a dozen people who provide the shared tools and infrastructure that iwoca’s engineering, data, and analytics teams rely on. You’ll be one of six engineers in the Platform team.

The role

As the Senior Platform Engineer, you’ll own the developer experience roadmap and agree with the team on where you can make the biggest impact for the platform’s users. You’ll decide how each self-service tool works and build it yourself, making clear trade-offs between developer experience, reliability, security, and cost. The tools you build help teams get code live faster which results in fewer support requests for the Platform team.

Today, getting a new service live takes many separate steps and a lot of platform knowledge. You’ll spend most of your time building new self-service tools, and the rest migrating existing tooling and talking to users about where they get stuck. If you haven’t worked deeply with Kubernetes, Terraform, or GitOps, you can learn them here, with the team and plenty of resources to help. You’ll likely start with the friction map below.

Live project examples:

  • Friction map. Measuring how long it takes someone outside Core Systems to get new code live, and how many steps they go through. The result could be written documentation or a dashboard.

  • New services. Turning the merge requests a new service needs into one guided flow, so fewer changes wait for review.

  • AI guardrails. Building the Claude skills and checks that help AI-written changes pass review and deploy cleanly first time.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Software engineering. You’ve written and maintained production code in Python or Go, including tools and automation.

  • Ownership. You’ve set the direction for a platform or tooling area and looked after it for the long term. You’ve decided what to fix first and seen the work through.

  • Building for internal users. You’ve built tooling and written documentation for other engineers, or for colleagues who aren’t engineers, and changed both based on how people used them.

  • AI leverage. You’ve used AI to produce work you couldn’t have delivered without it. You know where it speeds up changes, and where a change needs careful human review.

Bonus:

  • Kubernetes. You’ve deployed and debugged services on Kubernetes, and know its common resources and terms.

  • CI/CD and GitOps. You’ve built or maintained CI pipelines in GitLab CI or a similar system, and deployed services through a GitOps tool such as Flux or Argo CD.

  • Infrastructure as code. You’ve defined cloud resources in Terraform or a similar tool.

  • Delivery metrics. You’ve tracked measures such as lead time or deployment frequency, and used them to judge whether a change helped.

  • Developer environments. You’ve worked with cloud workspaces or devcontainers, and know what makes a developer environment pleasant to work in.

The salary

We expect to pay from £90,000 to £120,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

The GTM Performance & Strategy team helps teams turn strategy into consistent execution through targeted coaching, practice, and performance improvement. As a Senior Field Performance Partner, you’ll work with frontline Sales and Channel leaders across EMEA to diagnose performance gaps, build focused development plans, and use data and AI to help teams improve. Your work will help 1Password’s go-to-market organization perform at its best while advancing our mission to enable a safe, productive digital future.

This is not a traditional enablement role. We don’t believe more training is always the answer. We believe enablement should start with the performance problem, use data and AI to understand what’s happening, and apply the most targeted intervention possible.

You’ll independently own the performance improvement cycle for the teams you support: diagnose → prescribe → activate → reinforce → measure → adjust.

You’ll combine business results, AI-generated coaching insights, field observations, and manager input to identify where teams and individuals need support. You’ll turn those insights into focused enablement plans, use AI to scale individualized practice and coaching, help managers reinforce the right behaviors, and measure whether performance actually changed.

As 1Password continues to scale our partner-led GTM motion, you’ll also help make channel execution part of how our field operates every day. Rather than treating channel as a separate motion or specialist skill, you’ll help managers and teams build the behaviors needed to effectively identify, engage, and sell with partners as part of their everyday work.

Your job isn’t to keep people busy with enablement. It’s to help them perform better.

How we’re using AI today

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

Expectations of this role
This is a hybrid role. You will be expected to work from 1Password's London office 3 days per week, with the flexibility to work from the office up to 5 days based on business needs.

What we're looking for:

  • 7+ years of experience in a B2B technology GTM organization across Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, BDR, Enablement, frontline leadership, or a combination of these roles.

  • Experience working in a channel or partner-led GTM environment, with practical knowledge of selling with and through partners such as resellers, MSPs, distributors, and other channel partners, including partner engagement, account mapping, co-selling, and partner-led growth.

  • Experience carrying a quota, leading a frontline GTM team, or directly coaching customer-facing teams strongly preferred.

  • Strong business and analytical acumen, with demonstrated ability to diagnose performance problems, identify root causes, and turn insights into practical, measurable plans that improve skills, behaviors, and business outcomes.

  • Understanding of how to apply sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC in coaching, enablement, or field execution.

  • Credibility with frontline GTM leaders and sellers, built through curiosity, thoughtful discovery, and sound judgment, with the ability to operate independently as a coach, advisor, and constructive challenger.

  • High curiosity and fluency with AI, with experience using AI, automation, dashboards, and performance signals to make coaching more individualized, scalable, and measurable.

  • Understanding of how selling practices and customer needs vary across EMEA markets; additional language skills are helpful.

  • A bias toward action, experimentation, measurement, and continuous improvement.

What you can expect:

  • Own the performance improvement cycle for the frontline managers and teams you support: diagnose, prescribe, activate, reinforce, measure, and adjust.

  • Establish a consistent operating rhythm with managers, bringing data-informed insights and recommendations about where their coaching can have the greatest impact.

  • Combine business results, behavioral data, AI-generated coaching insights, field observations, and manager input to identify performance gaps and create focused development plans.

  • Create strategic enablement plans that address root causes and become part of the team’s day-to-day work.

  • Use AI-powered role-play, practice, feedback loops, manager coaching, live learning, and tools such as Hyperbound to support individualized development at scale.

  • Help managers reinforce key skills, products, messaging, partner motions, and GTM priorities through ongoing coaching and team practice.

  • Partner across Technical Enablement, Revenue Operations, Go-to-Market Engineering, and other teams to bring the right resources into identified performance challenges.

  • Facilitate workshops, webinars, and other learning experiences when appropriate, while enabling managers to lead reinforcement with their teams.

  • Measure whether interventions are changing behavior and improving outcomes, and share recurring performance patterns and field feedback with cross-functional partners.

This role is also eligible for immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, pension, and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.


Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. Founding Data Researcher
description:
TL;DR Davis is hiring a Founding Data Researcher to build the data behind our foundation model, trained from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. You will own the data end to end, from raw floorplans and synthetic generation to a canonical representation, curation, large-scale pretraining and the ablations that tell us which data actually moves the model. Here the dataset is part of the algorithm.

About Davis

Davis is an AI-native real estate company accelerating early-stage development and architectural design. Today developers coordinate four to five fragmented stakeholders over weeks or months. Soon they will need only one: Davis.

We turn every input that shapes a development decision into decision-ready outputs: investor-grade feasibility studies, investment analysis, and architect-certified designs, delivered in days. Every stage pairs our proprietary AI systems with expert review, so velocity never comes at the cost of reliability.

We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

The Role

You will own the data our foundation model learns from, a model we train from scratch to generate buildings as geometric graphs. Part of the corpus comes from real floorplans as images and PDFs that have to become clean, standardized graphs. A large part will be synthetic, procedurally generated building graphs, geometry and rendered floorplans, with controlled variation in style, scan noise, annotations and furniture, each kept with its ground-truth graph automatically.

You will think about the whole loop, from raw and synthetic data to a canonical structured representation, curation and validation, the training dataset, large-scale pretraining, evaluation, data ablations, and back to improving the generator and the data mixture. You are senior enough to architect the data stack and set the data strategy, and hands-on enough to write the pipelines, run the experiments, train the models and do the ablations yourself.

What you will be working on

  • Corpus from raw sources. Turn real floorplans (images, PDFs, scans) into clean, standardized building graphs, with the geometry and semantics that make them trainable.

  • Synthetic data generation. Explore strategies to expand the dataset with synthetic data.

  • Canonical representation and curation. Define the standardized representation, then filter, deduplicate, quality-score and validate at scale, with versioning, provenance and lineage.

  • Pretraining data and mixtures. Assemble the training datasets, design the mixture and the curriculum, and blend synthetic and real data for large-scale pretraining.

  • Data ablations. Train models to learn which data actually helps, read the results, and feed them back into the generator and the mixture.

  • Evaluation. Build the eval harness (datasets, metrics, regression tests, monitoring) that tracks data and model quality over time.

What We Are Looking For

  • You have built the dataset, not just trained on it. You have personally built or generated the data used for a large pretraining run, from raw or synthetic sources, rather than only training on a dataset someone handed you.

  • Senior and deeply hands-on. At least 5 years of strong experience, senior enough to architect the data stack and set strategy, but still coding the pipelines, running the experiments and doing the ablations yourself.

  • Data as a first-class problem. A track record where the data itself is the object: curation, filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixtures, synthetic generation.

  • Strong engineering. Deep Python, clean and typed code, async and concurrency, distributed data pipelines, TDD culture.

Nice to have

  • Computer vision and document understanding, images to structured output, OCR, layout extraction, segmentation, geometry extraction, vectorization, raster to vector, image to scene graph, 3D or CAD.

  • Graph and structured scientific data, molecular, protein or scene graphs, meshes, CAD, BIM, 3D geometry, or relational and structured world data.

  • Synthetic worlds and simulation, a structured state to a simulator to a renderer to synthetic images with perfect labels, then a perception model, with an eye on the sim-to-real gap.

  • Foundation models from scratch, real involvement in a large pretraining run, not only fine-tuning.

  • Public evidence of data ownership, lead on a dataset, a Hugging Face release, a dataset card, a technical blog on your pipeline, or a talk on data curation or synthetic data.

  • GIS and geometry, parcels, zoning layers, projections, computational geometry or constrained optimization.

  • Multi-country data, heterogeneous sources, localization and varying rules.

Why Join Davis

  • Own the data end to end, from the generator to the pretraining mixture, as the person who defines what the model learns from.

  • Shape a foundation model from scratch, on a structured representation no one else is training on.

  • Work on genuinely hard problems, image to graph, synthetic worlds and large-scale pretraining, with your work reaching clients within days.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity, at a founding level, in an early-stage company.

  • Join a world-class team, a mix of AI researchers, engineers and architects backed by world-class VCs.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we're going after:

Team

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He is a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we are a team of twelve: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise. We are small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you are the one we need.

Why We Will Win

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It did not work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We do not sell tools, we sell the work, AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability, and parametric tools only check constraints after generation, which leaves designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this, but does not yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. These layouts may look plausible yet break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they are usable.

This is exactly the gap Davis closes. Because our model generates on structured representations rather than pixels, it produces compliant, editable plans from the start, and the data you build feeds that model directly.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you are drawn to what we are building but do not meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet all of the criteria. If that is you, please do not let it hold you back. We would love to receive your application.

title: Senior Robotics Engineer
description:
About Inbolt

Deploying an industrial robot still takes months of integration and programming, and the moment a part, a process, or a position changes, it starts over. Inbolt makes it take minutes.

Our generalist vision model gives robots the ability to see, think, and adapt in real time, so any robot can master any process, part, or station. Set up from a CAD model in minutes and compatible with FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, Comau, and Universal Robots, Inbolt runs in production at Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, GM, Bosch, and more, with 200+ systems live across 100+ factories on three continents.

We're a team based in Paris, Detroit, and Japan, and we're growing fast. Here's the role:

This position is Paris, France based.

Role Overview

Your mission is to own the integration of complex robotics features into Inbolt Studio, at 100% industrial-grade quality, from architecture to production on the factory floor.

As Senior Robotics Engineer, you are the technical reference for robot control and robot programming in our product. Our roadmap covers static and dynamic robot control whatever the brand. You will architect and build these capabilities, integrate them end to end into Inbolt Studio, and make sure they run reliably on real robots in demanding production environments.

You will work at the intersection of robotics, 3D perception, and software engineering, in a small fast growing team where your contribution is visible and your decisions shape the product. This is not an R&D position: your work has a daily impact on what runs in production at Inbolt customers.

Want to take your robotics career to the next level by building the future of robot vision guidance in the real world? This role is for you.

Responsibilities

Feature ownership and architecture

  • Own the design and integration of complex robotics features into Inbolt Studio, from architecture to production release

  • Deliver the roadmap on static and dynamic robot control

  • Make the key technical decisions on motion planning, robot control, and real-time constraints, and defend them with data

  • Push the limits of the current codebase and propose better architectures when needed

Industrial-grade quality

  • Guarantee industrial-grade quality: every feature is tested, validated on real robots, robust to edge cases, and safe to run in a factory

  • Set the standards for code quality, testing, and review in the robotics team, and keep the PR process efficient

  • Own the quality of your deliverables: code, engineering reports, and validation results

  • Estimate lead times fairly for Epics, deliver on schedule, and flag early when a plan is drifting

From lab idea to production

  • Turn prototypes into production features, validated in real factory conditions at customer sites

  • Integrate and validate Inbolt’s solution across industrial robot brands and their programming environments

  • Keep a solid view of the state of the art in robotics, and bring what is relevant into the product

Technical leadership and collaboration

  • Act as the technical reference for the application engineering (RAE) and sales teams on complex customer cases, feasibility, and escalations

  • Review designs and code, mentor engineers, and take part in interviews for new hires

  • Work closely with the Lead Robotics engineer, other engineering teams, and deployment teams in Paris, the US, and Japan

Profile

Inbolt values end-to-end ownership, high rigor, and a hands-on curiosity. We move fast while staying precise, with a proactive, autonomous, results-driven mindset and strong collaboration with engineering teams.

Required Skills

  • 5+ years of strong professional experience in robotics, in a startup or a large company, with a track record of owning complex features end to end

  • Strong expertise in robotics motion planning: trajectory generation, path planning, collision avoidance, and motion optimization for industrial robot arms

  • Strong expertise in real-time robot control, both static and dynamic (sensor-driven): closed-loop control, low-latency sensor-to-motion pipelines, and deterministic, performance-critical code running on real robots

  • Excellence in software development: strong Python and/or C++, solid engineering practices (testing, code review, version control, CI/CD)

  • Proven record of shipping complex robotics features to production at industrial-grade quality: reliability, test strategy, and validation on real robots

  • Ability to design abstractions that work across robot brands and programming languages

  • Solid foundations in robotics: kinematics, frames and transformations, and integration with industrial or collaborative robot arms

  • Technical leadership: you make architecture decisions, raise the bar in code reviews, and mentor other engineers

  • Appetite for fast development and visible impact: you iterate quickly, ship often, and take ownership of the result

  • Clear communicator, able to explain technical topics to engineers, sales, and customers

  • Fluent in English; French is a big plus given daily interactions with the Paris team

Additional Plus

  • A PhD in robotics or a related field is appreciated, as long as your focus is on shipping: this role is about production impact, not research

  • Experience with 3D vision, point clouds, computer vision, or machine learning applied to perception

  • Experience with industrial robot brands (Universal Robots, ABB, FANUC, KUKA, Yaskawa, Comau) and their programming languages

  • Experience with ROS or other robotics frameworks

  • Experience deploying or supporting systems on customer sites in industrial environments

  • Experience as a tech lead or team lead of a robotics team

Position details

  • Role: Senior Robotics Engineer

  • Team: Engineering

  • Location: Paris, France, in our office at 12 rue Vivienne, 75002 Paris

  • Start date: ASAP

  • Employment type: Full-time

  • Collaboration: you will work closely with teams in Paris, the US, and Japan, and your work will directly impact deployments in factories worldwide

Why join Inbolt

  • Real impact, on real factory floors: your work runs in production at Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, GM, and Bosch, across 100+ factories on three continents.

  • Ownership from day one: we value end-to-end ownership, high rigor, and hands-on curiosity, and we move fast while staying precise.

  • An international team: Paris, Detroit, and Japan, working closely with world-class robotics and automation partners.

  • A seat at the start of something big: we're building the default intelligence layer for every industrial robot, on every brand.

Benefits

We're building our benefits location by location, so they fit local needs and practices in each country where we operate.

  • 📍 Prime office locations in Paris and Detroit

  • 🤝 Team-building events & off-sites

  • 🐶 Bring-your-dog-to-work policy

  • 🍽️ Lunch expenses covered

  • ✈️ Customer site visits in real factories

  • and more…

Benefits may vary by location and contract type.

Our hiring process

  • Introduction call (30 min) with our Talent team, to get to know you and answer your questions.

  • Interview with your future manager, including a case study or technical exercise depending on the role.

  • Meet the team: a conversation with the people you will work with every day.

  • Final round with our founders.

  • Reference checks.

The exact steps can vary slightly by role. We keep the process short and transparent, and we'll keep you posted at every step.

Ready to give robots sight?

Inbolt is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from everyone, whatever their background, and a real person reads every application. Even if you don't tick every box, if this role excites you, we'd love to hear from you.

title: AI Engineer
description:
Alassio recherche son (sa) prochain(e) AI Engineer !

 
 

Missions

 

🏗️ Alassio en quelques mots

En France, la paie et le social comptent parmi les fonctions les plus réglementées qui soient. Entre inflation réglementaire et évolutions légales et conventionnelles incessantes, la conformité est devenue un véritable fardeau pour les cabinets de paie et les services RH :

  • ce fardeau les empêche de se consacrer à ce qui compte vraiment, le conseil et l'accompagnement des salariés, qui en subissent donc eux aussi le poids

  • c'est aussi l'un des métiers où l'attrition est la plus forte en France, notamment parce que 60 % du temps des gestionnaires de paie est encore consacré à de la saisie ou à de la relecture manuelle

Pourtant, des solutions technologiques majeures existent : l'IA permet en particulier d'automatiser une très grande partie des tâches les plus pénibles et de valoriser les données sociales. Mais le secteur reste largement à l'écart de cette révolution, et le problème n'est pas seulement réglementaire : le marché était verrouillé par des éditeurs historiques vieillissants, difficiles à quitter faute d'alternative crédible et de moyens pour migrer efficacement. Là aussi, l'IA fait voler ces barrières en éclats et ouvre la voie à une vague d'innovation attendue depuis des décennies.

C'est pour y répondre qu'Alassio construit la plateforme de paie et de gestion RH moderne qui manquait à ce marché, au service des cabinets et de leurs clients TPE/PME. Notre ambition est de développer en un temps record :

  • une plateforme collaborative et ouverte, qui s'intègre nativement aux outils des cabinets et de leurs clients, respecte leurs habitudes de travail et fluidifie les échanges entre gestionnaires de paie et entreprises

  • l'automatisation de la tenue administrative : collecte des données, paramétrage des évolutions légales et des règles propres à chaque entreprise, génération automatique des rapports et formulaires, traçabilité juridique dynamique et en temps réel, etc.

  • la valorisation des données de paie et sociales, pour offrir un conseil social à 360° et enfin répondre efficacement à l'ensemble des attentes des salariés, qui se sont de surcroît largement amplifiées depuis le Covid : gestion contractuelle, pilotage de la masse salariale, avantages salariés, fidélisation des talents, mutuelle…

L'objectif : devenir le « People OS » sur lequel les cabinets et leurs clients TPE/PME s'appuient pour gérer l'intégralité de leurs problématiques paie et RH.

 

🚀 Tes responsabilités

Ta mission : faire de l'IA le levier qui démultiplie le travail de chacun chez Alassio. L'objectif est assumé : multiplier par 10 la productivité de chaque membre de l'équipe.

  • Tu formes la Growth squad avec notre Founding Strategy & Operations : ce binôme transverse optimise l'existant, automatise les workflows de toutes les équipes et fait passer nos initiatives IA et nos outils internes à l'échelle : hébergement et mise en production dans des environnements partagés, sécurité, observabilité, optimisation et amélioration continue

  • Tu deviens le (la) référent(e) IA d'Alassio : on se veut profondément AI-native et on expérimente énormément. Tu centralises et coordonnes ces initiatives pour que ce "lab interne" soit efficace, et tu expérimentes aussi en continu avec toutes les techno IA (budget et outillage conséquents)

  • Tu construis la nouvelle colonne vertébrale IT d'Alassio, en identifiant les systèmes IA qui comptent à l'échelle de toute l'entreprise

  • Tu prépares l'avenir du produit : à terme, les usages testés et éprouvés en interne sous ton impulsion ont vocation à rejoindre notre plateforme. Ils nourriront le « People OS » qui démocratise les cas d'usage les plus pertinents de l'IA dans notre secteur

 

🧭 Tes premiers chantiers

Ton point de départ : Bedrock, notre OS interne. Un peu à la manière de Palantir Foundry, il agrège & orchestre tout le contexte de l'entreprise pour en tirer des actions concrètes : suivi ultra-personnalisé et automatisé de nos utilisateurs, analyse produit, documentation, rédaction de tickets et PR associées…

Bedrock est déjà au cœur du quotidien de toutes les équipes. Mais il s'est construit par couches successives, au fil des cas d'usage ajoutés. Ton premier objectif est d'en dresser l'inventaire complet, process et outils IA compris. Tu définis ensuite la roadmap qui le fera changer de dimension :

  • Workflows : optimiser l'existant

  • Infrastructure : sécurité, confidentialité, hébergement et environnements partagés, pour un OS multi-joueur, plug-and-play et scalable

  • Observabilité : suivre les agents et leur performance, et améliorer chaque logique en continu

  • Autonomie : construire des workflows agentiques déclenchés par webhook ou planifiés, qui nettoient le contexte et mènent des missions 24/7

Très vite, tu as vocation à devenir le (la) responsable qui orchestre l'IA chez Alassio, et le (la) référent(e) de notre OS Bedrock.

 
 

Profil recherché

 

🌱 Expérience

  • 1 à 2 ans d'expérience dans un rôle d'AI Engineer / FDE / AI Deployment Strategist dans une top structure tech (BCGX, Palantir, Dust)

  • Plusieurs missions concrètes de déploiement et d'optimisation de technologies IA : mise en place de zéro d'un workflow au sein d'une organisation, sujets de gouvernance et de déploiement en entreprise, etc.

  • Une utilisation intensive des outils IA et une bonne maîtrise de Python : Claude Code / Codex ; Cursor Agents, Linear/PostHog, déploiement et hébergement (cloud, AI routers, etc.)

 

💎 Qualités

  • Penser à l'échelle : tu conçois dès le départ des solutions capables d'encaisser des montées en charge ×10 ou ×100, tout en restant pragmatique sur ce qui compte à court et moyen terme

Tu rejoins une aventure entrepreneuriale en plein passage à l'échelle, sur un marché verrouillé depuis des années. Le marché de la paie en cabinet d'expertise comptable est dominé depuis des décennies par des solutions historiques. Chez Alassio, notre ambition est de rénover le métier au bénéfice des gestionnaires de paie, avec un logiciel moderne, évolutif et pensé pour les réalités du terrain.

Changer de logiciel de paie est un projet lourd pour un cabinet. La réussite de chaque migration est décisive : c'est elle qui fait d'un cabinet signé un cabinet convaincu, puis un ambassadeur. Pour accompagner l'arrivée de nouveaux cabinets, nous renforçons l'équipe Déploiement & Accompagnement (DnA), qui assure un suivi actif de chacun de nos cabinets partenaires.

Ce poste est le premier recrutement de l’équipe DnA. Profil recherché

2️⃣ Entretien métier avec Alexandre et Huy Anh (Resp. Métier) : 45 min

4️⃣ Rencontre informelle avec l'équipe : 1 h

👉 Le processus se termine par des prises de référence.
